definitions.definition: an official record showing that you have finished a training course or have the necessary skills, etc.:

definitions.definition: an ability, characteristic, or experience that makes you suitable for a particular job or activity:

definitions.definition: an ability, characteristic, or experience that makes you suitable for a particular job or activity:

definitions.definition: based on information that cannot be easily measured, such as people's opinions and feelings, rather than on information that can be shown in numbers:

definitions.definition: how good or bad something is:

definitions.definition: a likelihood to happen or to have a particular characteristic or effect:

definitions.definition: gentle, loving, or kind:

definitions.definition: to cover something with a tent or similar structure:

definitions.definition: not certain or agreed:

definitions.definition: said or done in a careful way because you do not know if you are right:

definitions.definition: one of the periods into which a year is divided at school, college, or university:

definitions.definition: a number or symbol used in a mathematical series or calculation:

definitions.definition: a period of time during which something lasts:

definitions.definition: the period of time during which someone is in a job or position, or that a government is in power:

definitions.definition: a word or expression used in relation to a particular subject, often for something official or technical:

definitions.definition: one of the conditions of an agreement, arrangement, or activity:

definitions.definition: saying something in a particular way:

definitions.definition: for a long, medium or short period of time in the future:

definitions.definition: to use a particular word or expression to describe something:

definitions.definition: extreme, when referring to something unpleasant or negative:

definitions.definition: causing something to end or fail:

definitions.definition: to (cause something to) end or stop:

definitions.definition: to end or stop, or to cause something to end or stop:

definitions.definition: to end or to make something end:

definitions.definition: to remove someone from their job:

definitions.definition: very unpleasant or serious or of low quality:

definitions.definition: very bad at doing something:

definitions.definition: used to emphasize the great degree of something:

definitions.definition: very unpleasant or serious or bad:

definitions.definition: very good:

definitions.definition: extreme fear, or violent action that causes fear:

definitions.definition: to perform in a particular way when answering a set of questions:

definitions.definition: to be judged in a particular way when used somewhere or shown to someone:

definitions.definition: to ask someone a set of questions or give them practical activities to do, in order to measure their knowledge or ability:

definitions.definition: to do something in order to discover if something is safe, works correctly, etc., or if something is present:

definitions.definition: if a situation tests someone or something, it shows how good, strong, etc. they are:
definitions.example: The new chief executive will quickly get a chance to test his diplomatic skills.

definitions.definition: (of a person) to speak seriously about something, especially in a law court, or to give or provide proof:

definitions.definition: (of a fact, event, etc.) to show something or prove that something is true:

definitions.example: After texting a code number, users will be able to launch the web-based application on their mobile screen.

definitions.definition: (of an example of something) extremely good, or thought to be usual or typical:
definitions.example: That was a textbook play by the defense.

definitions.definition: cloth made by hand or machine in large quantities:

definitions.definition: the quality of something that can be decided by touch, for example whether it is rough or smooth, or soft or hard:

definitions.example: He wrote more than 20 books.

definitions.definition: used to express a reaction to something:
definitions.example: I didn't know she'd been so sick. That's terrible.

definitions.definition: as much as suggested:

definitions.definition: as much as suggested:

definitions.example: Her mind was in turmoil.

definitions.definition: to move in a circle around a fixed point or line, or to make something move in this way:
definitions.example: The wheels started to turn.

definitions.definition: to perform a movement in which your body moves around in a circle:
definitions.example: She turned a full somersault in the air.

definitions.definition: to change the direction in which you are facing or moving, or to make someone or something do this:
definitions.example: Turn right at the traffic lights.

definitions.definition: In cricket, if a ball turns, it changes direction suddenly when it hits the ground:
definitions.example: On this field, the ball turns and our batsmen have had to learn a new technique

definitions.definition: to move, or to move an object or a page, so that a different side or surface is on the top:
definitions.example: Now turn the page, please, and start work on exercise 2.

definitions.definition: to become, change into, or come to be something, or to make this happen:
definitions.example: The weather has suddenly turned cold.

definitions.definition: to shape a piece of wood while it is attached to a machine that spins it:
definitions.example: I turn posts and spindles for new and replacement staircases.

definitions.definition: to move or cause something to move in a circle around a central point or line:
definitions.example: The earth turns on its axis once every 24 hours.

definitions.definition: to change the direction in which you are facing or moving, or to cause someone or something to face or move in a different direction:
definitions.example: They told us to turn right at the first traffic light.

definitions.definition: If you turn something or turn something over, you place the surface that was on top on the bottom:
definitions.example: He turned the pages of a magazine.

definitions.definition: to become or cause to become, change, or come to be:
definitions.example: The weather suddenly turned colder, and it started to rain.

definitions.definition: to use a control to switch a piece of equipment on or off, or to adjust it to change the amount of what it is producing:
definitions.example: Please turn off/out the lights when you leave.

definitions.definition: to change into something or make something change into something:
definitions.example: These machines can turn a computer design into a 3-D prototype in minutes.

definitions.definition: to change direction, or to make something change direction:
definitions.example: The first quarter could see a further decline in retail customers, though executives said they were confident the trend will turn.

definitions.definition: an opportunity or a duty to do something at a particular time or in a particular order, before or after other people:
definitions.example: Is it my turn yet?

definitions.definition: a change in the direction in which you are moving or facing:
definitions.example: When you see the school on the left, make a right turn.

definitions.definition: starting to become better or worse:
definitions.example: There are fears that the housing market is on the turn.

definitions.definition: (of food or drink) starting to decay:
definitions.example: This milk smells funny – I think it's on the turn.

definitions.definition: the middle point in a round of golf, usually after the ninth hole:
definitions.example: He was six under at the turn.

definitions.definition: a slight illness, a strange feeling, or a nervous shock:
definitions.example: After the accident I started having funny turns.

definitions.definition: a change in the way something such as prices, rates, or the economy is behaving:
definitions.example: It is too early to know whether the economy has reached a turn in the cycle.

definitions.definition: the amount of time taken for something to happen after a vehicle, an instruction, or an order for goods arrives at a place:
definitions.example: We'll have to improve the turnaround - three days is too long.

definitions.definition: a big change that turns a bad situation into a good one:
definitions.example: The insurance group's focus on new products played a big part in its turnaround.

definitions.definition: the amount of business that a company does in a period of time:
definitions.example: Large supermarkets have high turnovers (= their goods sell very quickly).

definitions.definition: the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced by new people:
definitions.example: The large number of temporary contracts resulted in a high turnover of staff.

definitions.definition: in sports such as basketball, football, and rugby, the act of losing control of the ball and having the other team gain possession:
definitions.example: The Hawks committed a costly turnover in the fourth quarter.

definitions.definition: the amount of money that a company gets from sales during a particular period:
definitions.example: Group turnover rose 2% in the period, compared with last year.

definitions.definition: the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced by new employees:
definitions.example: The company has a staff turnover of around 12% a year.

definitions.definition: the total number and value of shares bought and sold on a stock market in a particular period of time:
definitions.example: The market dropped in heavy turnover.

definitions.definition: a teacher who teaches a student outside school, especially in order to give them extra help with a subject they find difficult:
definitions.example: His parents got him a tutor to help with his math.

definitions.definition: In the U.K. and some other countries, a teacher at a college or university who teaches one student or a small group and may also be responsible for giving help and advice to students on personal matters :
definitions.example: He was painstaking with less able students, encouraging and demanding with gifted ones and serious about a university tutor's pastoral responsibilities.

definitions.definition: a teacher at a school who is responsible for giving help and advice to a student or group of students on school and personal matters:
definitions.example: Your form tutor will take the register each day.

definitions.definition: abbreviation for television:
definitions.example: We ate in front of (= while watching) the TV.

definitions.definition: the number 12:
definitions.example: The cafeteria opens for lunch at twelve (o'clock).
Casey is twelve.

definitions.definition: the number 20:
definitions.example: nineteen, twenty, twenty-one
She’s twenty years old.

definitions.definition: two times:
definitions.example: I've already asked him twice.

definitions.definition: two times:
definitions.example: Take the medicine twice a day.

definitions.definition: either of two children born to the same mother on the same occasion:
definitions.example: My sister has twin sons.

definitions.definition: used to describe two similar things that are a pair:
definitions.example: twin towers

definitions.definition: to put something together with something else, especially because they work well as a pair:
definitions.example: She twins a shimmering silk blouse with a dark wool skirt.

definitions.definition: If two towns, organizations, etc. are twinned, or one is twinned with the other, a connection or special relationship is established between them:
definitions.example: Cambridge is twinned with Heidelberg.

definitions.definition: (of light or a shiny surface) to shine repeatedly strongly then weakly, as if flashing on and off very quickly:
definitions.example: The lights of the town twinkled in the distance.

definitions.definition: an act of twinkling:
definitions.example: the twinkle of the stars/lights/diamonds

definitions.definition: a flash of light, shining brightly and then less brightly:
definitions.example: We could see the twinkle of lights across the bay

definitions.definition: to turn something, especially repeatedly, or to turn or wrap one thing around another:
definitions.example: The path twists and turns for over a mile.

definitions.definition: to change information so that it gives the message you want it to give, especially in a way that is dishonest:
definitions.example: This report shows how she twisted the truth to claim successes where none, in fact, existed.

definitions.definition: to turn repeatedly, or to combine thin lengths of a material by turning or wrapping:
definitions.example: A river twists through the valley.

definitions.definition: to change the meaning of facts or a statement; distort:
definitions.example: You’re twisting my words – that’s not what I meant at all.

definitions.definition: an act of twisting something:
definitions.example: She gave the cap another twist to make sure it was tight.

definitions.definition: the shape of or a piece of something that has been twisted:
definitions.example: Long twists of grey hair fell over her face.

definitions.definition: in sports such as diving and gymnastics, a movement in which a person turns their whole body while in the air :
definitions.example: The dive includes two-and-a-half somersaults with two-and-a-half twists.

definitions.definition: a change in the way in which something happens:
definitions.example: The story took a surprise twist today with media reports that the doctor had resigned.

definitions.definition: a complicated situation or plan of action:
definitions.example: the twists and turns of fate

definitions.definition: the act of twisting or turning repeatedly:
definitions.example: The path wound its way down the hill in a series of twists.

definitions.definition: an unexpected change:
definitions.example: The incident was the latest twist in the story of the robbery.

definitions.definition: the number 2:
definitions.example: They have two houses.
Josh’ll be two in February.

definitions.definition: a particular group of people or things that share similar characteristics and form a smaller division of a larger set:
definitions.example: There were so many different types of bread that I didn't know which to buy.

definitions.definition: the style and size of printed letters used in a piece of printed writing such as in a newspaper, book, or article:
definitions.example: Use bold type for your headings.

definitions.definition: the characteristics of a group of people or things that set them apart from other people or things, or people, things, or groups that share particular characteristics:
definitions.example: I’m more comfortable in jeans and T-shirts, and that type of thing.

definitions.definition: to write using a machine, either a computer keyboard or a typewriter:
definitions.example: She asked me to type a couple of letters.

definitions.definition: to write using a keyboard:
definitions.example: I never learned how to type.

definitions.definition: to write using a computer keyboard or a typewriter:
definitions.example: How fast can you type?

definitions.definition: a machine with keys that you press to produce letters and numbers on paper:
definitions.example: He still uses an old typewriter.

definitions.definition: showing all the characteristics that you would usually expect from a particular group of things:
definitions.example: I must look like the typical tourist with my shorts and my camera.

definitions.definition: showing all the bad characteristics that you expect from someone or something, often in a way that is annoying:
definitions.example: It's just typical of Dan to spend all that money on the equipment and then lose interest two months later.

definitions.definition: showing the characteristics of a particular kind of person or thing:
definitions.example: He looked like the typical tourist with his camera and baseball cap.

definitions.definition: in a way that shows all the characteristics that you would expect from the stated person, thing, or group:
definitions.example: She has that reserve and slight coldness of manner which is typically English.

definitions.definition: used when you are giving an average or usual example of a particular thing:
definitions.example: Typically, a doctor will see about 30 patients a day.

definitions.definition: in a way that shows the characteristics of a particular kind of person or thing, or gives a usual example of a particular thing:
definitions.example: It’s a typically American town.
